This keeps uniform per-column workload (so static scheduling should balance well) and, crucially, preserves the same summation order as the original algorithm, meaning the floating-point results should match exactly without needing any tolerance.\n\nI'm also checking that the in-place update pattern still works—column j's entries stay untouched until processed, and the original's diagonal index j as the original, since both versions compute diagonals in the same row/column order.\n\nFor parallelism, I'm estimating the work per column is roughly O(j) iterations, giving n³/6 total multiply-adds, with the sequential diagonal step being negligible overhead for reasonable n.\n\nTo reduce fork/join overhead, I'm thinking of restructuring to wrap the whole column loop in one parallel region, using a single construct for the diagonal computation (with its implicit barrier) and an omp for for the off-diagonal work, then handling the failure flag carefully so all threads break out uniformly after the barrier rather than trying to return from inside the parallel region.\n\nMemory access per column j touches row i of L for i>j alongside row j itself, so the working set at each column is roughly (n-j)*j doubles, which matters for cache behavior at n=512.\n\nI'm estimating total memory traffic for the column-wise approach: summing (n-j)*j across all columns gives roughly n^3/3 accesses, around 357MB for n=512, which should mostly stay within L3 cache but it's still bandwidth-heavier than a blocked algorithm, and the dot products here aren't vectorizing well L[j][j] = sqrt(A[j][j] - sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2)            (serial, O(j))\n//   2. L[i][j] = (A[i][j] - sum_{k<j} L[i][k] * L[j][k]) / L[j][j]\n//      for all i > j                                              (parallel)\n// Every entry is accumulated over k in the same increasing order as the\n// original row-oriented algorithm, so results are bitwise identical.\n// Rows are processed in blocks of 4 to give the CPU independent accumulation\n// chains (ILP) without changing any per-element summation order.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* const a = A.data();\n    bool ok = true;\n\n#pragma omp parallel shared(ok)\n    {\n        for (size_t j = 0;
